# v0.49.86

This patch fixes a crash of the Magic Context sidebar in the OpenCode terminal, and makes the nightly memory check cover code inside git submodules.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode terminal: the sidebar could crash after a status refresh** (issue 987, thanks @iceteaSA for the report and the fix). The sidebar read some status values without checking that they were present. When a refresh delivered a status without one of them, the sidebar crashed. It now checks every status value before it uses it and leaves out a part whose value is missing.
- **The nightly memory check skipped memories about code in git submodules** (issue 973, thanks @AyhamJo7 for the fix). To check a memory against the code, Magic Context lists the files that git tracks. That list did not include files inside submodules, so a memory about such a file was never checked, while the run still reported itself as complete. The list now includes the files of submodules. This applies to OpenCode, Pi and Oh My Pi.

# v0.49.85

This patch fixes a crash at exit on Pi that could happen while a local embedding was being computed, and makes startup faster for stores with many files.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **Pi: the process could abort at exit while a local embedding was running** (issue 995, thanks @chpock). With the local embedding provider, Magic Context computes embeddings in a worker that calls a native library. When Pi shut down, Magic Context stopped that worker at once, also in the middle of a native call, and Pi's shutdown did not wait for it. Under Node the process then ended with `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'Napi::Error'` and exit code 134 in place of a normal exit. In our reproduction on Node 26 this happened in 18 of 20 exits that had an embedding in flight. Now stopping the worker is a request. The worker finishes the call it is running, starts no further one, releases the model and ends by itself, and Pi's shutdown waits for that. The wait was 10 to 310 ms in the test runs. The same holds for a worker that a configuration or model change retired shortly before the exit.
- **Oh My Pi:** the same abort happened on Bun in a few of 20 such exits. It is fixed by the same change.
- **A worker that does not stop is bounded.** If a worker does not end within 5 seconds, it is terminated as before, and a stop always settles within about 7 seconds. One log line says that the worker was terminated and whether an embedding was running.

OpenCode itself was not at risk: there the worker runs in a child process. That child is now asked to stop in the same way and is no longer killed in the middle of a call.

- **Startup checked the permissions of every file in the storage folder, twice** (issue 878, thanks @iceteaSA for the report and the fix). On the first database open in a process, Magic Context checked every entry under its storage folder, on the main thread, two times. A store with thousands of files made startup slow. Now a clean full check leaves a private marker in the storage folder. While the marker is valid, a start checks only the storage folder, the database files and the `models/` and `logs/` folders: 7 file checks in a test fixture that needed 2,004 before. The marker is valid for 24 hours and only when it holds the current rule version. Any wrong mode, an unusable marker, or a start with enforcement off removes it, and the next start does the full check again. A file that becomes readable by others after a clean check is repaired at the next full check, at most 24 hours later. The plugin still skips permission repair on Windows. A storage folder that is a symbolic link is followed as before; the permission check does not follow links, so it reports such a folder in the log and does not skip the full check for it.

## Known limit

An exit that does not go through the host's own shutdown, such as a fatal error or another extension that calls `process.exit`, can still abort under Node when an embedding is running at that moment. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D, `/quit`, SIGTERM and SIGHUP in Pi's interactive mode go through the shutdown and are covered.

## Changed

- When a running embedding worker is stopped, the log has one line with the process id, whether an embedding was running, and how long the stop took: `[magic-context] embedding worker stopped (…)`.
- Embedding results and the speed of a normal embedding request are unchanged.

# v0.49.84

This patch fixes three faults on OpenCode 2: the saved model list lost image support and limits after the first reply, so the memory mural never rendered; an undo left records behind for the messages it removed; and a storage notice could reach the model or end a turn early.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

**If you use the memory mural (`mural.enabled`) on OpenCode 2 with a text-only model that you defined yourself:** the mural now works on OpenCode 2, and Magic Context takes the host's word for which models accept images. OpenCode 2 lists a model that you define without `capabilities` as accepting text and images. For a text-only model, set `capabilities.input` to `["text"]` on that model in your OpenCode config. Otherwise the mural image is sent to it, and a server that refuses images will refuse the request.

## Fixed

- **OpenCode 2: every model was saved as not accepting images, so the memory mural never rendered** (issue 993, thanks @mgt-l). Magic Context keeps a list of each model's limits and whether it accepts images. At start it fills that list from the host's full model catalog. After the first reply of a session it refreshed the list, kept only the limits of each model, and replaced the whole list with the result. Every model then read as text-only, and the mural was skipped without a log line. Models that the refresh did not list were removed with their limits, and a session on such a model used a detected limit or a 200,000-token default until a later refresh. The fault was in every release since 0.43.0. Now the refresh adds to the list: a model that the refresh does not list stays as it was, a listed model takes the host's current limits, and image support changes only when the host states which inputs the model accepts. A model defined in a project, which the plugin first sees at the first reply, gets its image support there. A list that is already damaged repairs itself at the next start or the next first reply; you do not need to delete a file. OpenCode 1 and Pi did not have the fault.
- **OpenCode 2: an undo left records for the removed messages** (issue 988, thanks @null-axiom). When you undo messages in OpenCode 2 and then continue, the host deletes those messages. Magic Context kept their tags, its per-message records and its saved copy of the last request. The stale tags were counted in status, and the next request could log a false warning that the request had changed. Now, when the undo is committed, Magic Context removes its records for exactly the messages the host deleted. It deletes only for messages it saw before the undo and no longer finds after it. If it cannot prove which messages were removed, for example after a restart between the undo and the commit, it leaves the records in place and logs why. A session without an undo sends the same bytes as before.
- **OpenCode 2: summary rebuild data could outlive the summaries it belonged to** (issue 988). When an undo retires summaries, data staged for a summary rebuild is discarded with them.
- **OpenCode 2: a storage notice could reach the model or end a turn early.** When Magic Context cannot use its own store, it puts a notice for you into the conversation. The model must never read it, and the notice must not start a reply. Three faults were found on all four supported OpenCode 2 versions. A side question asked after a notice carried the notice text to the model. A notice that arrived while a tool was running ended the turn before the model saw the tool's result. A fork sent copies of earlier notices to the model. Now side questions and forks leave the notices out, and a turn that has a tool result or a new prompt continues. A notice that arrives in an idle session still starts no reply. A fork that has been sending copied notices rewrites its prompt cache once after the update, from the first copied notice on.

## Changed

-

releases.body:
## Added

- **A copy of your settings is kept before every save.** When you save in the Config editor, the dashboard first copies the file it replaces to `config-backups` in the Magic Context data folder. It keeps the newest 5 copies of each config. To go back, copy one over the config file. If the copy cannot be made, the save is refused. On macOS and Linux the copies are readable only by you; on Windows they inherit the permissions of the Magic Context data folder. Thanks to the contributor of pull request 959 (issue 956).

## Fixed

- **Large sessions open faster.** On a session with thousands of summaries and tens of thousands of messages, the Messages view received about 400 MB of data and built every summary's text at once. It now receives only the fields it shows (about 97% less in our test session), looks up summary times in batches, and builds a summary's text only when you expand it. In our test session the first frame of the Summaries view came in about half the time, and a filtered Messages view in about a fifth (issue 991).
- **Leaving the session list no longer keeps loading it.** A page of sessions that was still loading when you moved to another view could go on loading further pages in the background.
- **Model discovery no longer starts OpenCode from a temporary folder.** In two rare cases (a blank or relative data folder setting, and a home folder of `/`), the dashboard could still run its OpenCode checks from a temporary folder or from the AppImage mount. It now skips the check when it has no safe folder. Thanks to the contributor of pull request 986 (issue 985).

No settings change. The update arrives through the in-app updater.

# v0.49.83

This patch fixes three nightly maintenance faults: a retrospective that could read the same messages again every night, a daily run that did nothing for small projects, and file mapping that retried the same memory every day.

## Upgrading

Update the plugin with `npx @cortexkit/magic-context@latest doctor`, then restart your host. No database migration is needed.

## Fixed

- **The retrospective could re-read the same window every night** (issue 990, thanks @null-axiom). The retrospective reads your recent messages for friction and writes lessons as memories, then stores how far it has read. When a run hit one of its limits (80 new messages per session, 240 per run, the prompt budget, or more sessions than one run reads), it moved the stored position back to just before the first message it had not finished, but it still sent later messages to the model. The next run then received the same messages again and could write the same lessons again. Now a run that sends messages stores a position at or after the newest message it sent, and messages that share one timestamp are sent together or not at all. A position that is already stuck moves on the first run after the update. A group of messages with one timestamp that can never fit in a run is skipped, with a log line that says how many.
- **Importance scoring ran every day for projects with fewer than 10 memories and did nothing** (issue 989, thanks @null-axiom). The task needs at least 10 memories to work, but its schedule check and its backlog count did not apply that minimum. Such a project showed a backlog that never cleared and had one empty run per day. The check and the count now use the same minimum as the task.
- **File mapping tried a memory it could not link to any file again every day** (issue 989, thanks @null-axiom). File mapping links a memory to the files that back it, so the nightly check knows when to look at it again. A memory that matches no file was tried again after at most 24 hours, without end, one model call each time. Now the wait keeps doubling up to 7 days, and a change to the memory's text or category makes it eligible at once. Only a real "no file found" answer counts as a failed try: a provider error, a timeout or a run that could not start no longer lengthens the wait, and one run counts a memory once. A memory that is waiting no longer counts as backlog and no longer starts a run.

## Changed

- Every completed retrospective run now logs the position it started from, the newest message it read, the position it stored and the position it read back. If a retrospective ever seems stuck again, that line shows which step lost the advance.
